finding.source: V3 BOUNDARY instrument matrix (v3-boundary-instruments.json, ASan failures[1])
finding.symptom: LeakSanitizer: Direct leak of 84 byte(s) in 1 object(s); SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: 84 byte(s) leaked in 1 allocation(s). The test's assertions all passed.
finding.note_on_path: V3 named src/provider/fetch.rs:1134; the tree's file is src/evp/fetch.rs:1134. Same function (`inner_evp_generic_fetch`) and same call.

what_was_leaked.precise_object: One per-slot owned data buffer: the 83-character fetch-failure message formatted by inner_evp_generic_fetch plus its NUL (84 bytes), allocated by message_copy -> slot_buf_alloc (CRYPTO_malloc at (NULL, 0)) and stored in the thread's ERR_STATE slot with ERR_TXT_MALLOCED | ERR_TXT_STRING.
what_was_leaked.state_that_owned_it: The thread-local STATE (ERR_STATE) at src/runtime/err.rs. The ERR_STATE block itself is thread-local storage, not a heap allocation, so it is not an LSan object; the container Vec PENDING_RELEASES was empty at exit. The other two buffers of the same entry (err_file/err_func) had already been released by an ERR_clear_error on the path (clear frees debug strings but, with deall=false, keeps and truncates a MALLOCED data buffer), which is why exactly one 84-byte object remained.
what_was_leaked.root_cause: STATE was `UnsafeCell<ErrState>`, which needs no drop, so `thread_local!` registered no destructor. Nothing ran the authority's per-thread ERR_STATE teardown when the thread ended, so buffers the ring still owned at exit were never handed to CRYPTO_free.
what_was_leaked.authority_behaviour_preserved: The OpenSSL error queue is per-thread, bounded (15 usable slots in a 16-slot ring) and released when the thread ends. The fix restores the last element: the state's owned buffers are released at thread exit through the same seam and at the same err_local.h release coordinates; the state block itself is TLS and needs no release.

fix.mechanism: Wrap the thread-local cell in `struct StateCell(UnsafeCell<ErrState>)` with a `Drop` that runs the authority's own `OSSL_ERR_STATE_free` opening move, `ErrState::clear_all(true)`. `thread_local!` now registers a destructor (const init with a Drop type uses std's EagerStorage path, which registers and runs the dtor). The enclosing block is deliberately not freed: it is the TLS object. `ERR_get_state` reaches the state through `s.0.get()`; its signature, the `#[repr(C)]` layout and the stable per-thread address are unchanged.
fix.exactly_once: Every release path NULLs the slot it released: clear()/clear_data() free and NULL err_data/err_file/err_func, OSSL_ERR_STATE_save() and save_to_mark() move pointers out and zero the thread state, and ERR_clear_error()/ERR_pop()/ERR_get_error() keep a MALLOCED data buffer but truncate it in place. A thread-exit clear therefore frees each block exactly once, and running it after any explicit clear frees only what the clear left owned. No path frees the same block twice.
fix.reentrancy: Slot releases go through dso_shared::crypto_free, which may run an application free hook. During StateCell::drop the TLS key is already in std's Destroyed state, so a hook that re-enters ERR observes ERR_get_state == NULL and with_state refuses; it can never form a second reference to the state being released. SlotStr::drop's borrow-flag check reads STATE_IN_USE (a no-Drop Cell that stays readable), which is false because no with_state frame can survive into TLS teardown; even the pathological queueing arm would be flushed by PENDING_RELEASES' own destructor, which is registered later and therefore runs earlier.

regression_test.name: runtime::err::tests::err_thread_exit_releases_the_queued_data_buffer
regression_test.method: A spawned thread raises `raise_site_dynamic_data(EVP_FETCH_376, ...)`, reads the address of the owned data buffer from the live ERR_STATE (public repr(C) layout), and arms a test-only seam observer for that one address. A test-side thread-local reporter is initialized before the first ERR call, so its destructor runs after the state's (std's TLS destructors run LIFO); the main thread waits for that report and then asserts the exact address was passed to CRYPTO_free. Assertion is by address identity, not by counting releases in a window.
regression_test.pre_fix_control: With `StateCell::drop` temporarily made a no-op, the test fails: "the per-thread error state must release the buffer at 0x... it still owned at thread exit". With the destructor restored it passes. The experiment was reverted before the gates.
regression_test.seam_hook: src/runtime/dso_shared.rs: `note_free` now receives the released pointer under `#[cfg(test)]`; an AtomicUsize/AtomicBool pair records one armed address. No test-only code is compiled into a release build.

discharged: The per-thread error state's thread-exit release obligation: every owned slot buffer now has exactly one release path and it runs at thread end.
The new unsafe expression carries an explicit validity contract; safe callers cannot cause UB through it.
retained: StateCell::drop runs under no explicit borrow guard by construction: it cannot form a second reference because ERR_get_state answers NULL once the TLS key is Destroyed. This argument is documented at the Drop site and exercised by the new test, but not model-checked (no Miri run here).
